title: Selling and Promotion - Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA - Selling: Features & Benefits
subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: A salesperson says, 'This laptop has a 16-core processor and 32 gigabytes of RAM.' This statement is describing the product's:
options: Benefits
Features
Promotional mix
Institutional role
questions.explain: Features are physical, tangible, or factual characteristics of a product. In this case, the processor and RAM are facts about the laptop.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: If a feature is that a winter coat is lined with down feathers, what is the corresponding benefit?
options: The coat weighs 2.5 pounds.
The coat comes in four different colors.
The coat will keep the wearer warm in sub-zero temperatures.
The coat is imported from overseas.
questions.explain: A benefit is the personal value or utility a customer gets from a feature. Warmth is the result of the down feather feature.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: What is the core principle of 'feature-benefit selling'?
options: Listing as many technical specifications as possible until the customer buys.
Tying the factual attributes of a product to the specific personal advantages they offer the buyer.
Selling features separately from the main product to increase profits.
Focusing purely on the emotional state of the customer without mentioning the product.
questions.explain: Feature-benefit selling requires translating factual product attributes (features) into value and utility (benefits) that satisfy the buyer's motives.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Warranties, delivery policies, and financing options are generally categorized as:
options: Tangible product features
Extended product features
Customer liabilities
Institutional promotions
questions.explain: Extended product features add value to a product but are not part of the physical product itself. Warranties and financing are prime examples.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Which of the following is considered an emotional buying motive rather than a rational buying motive?
options: Purchasing a car because of its high fuel efficiency.
Purchasing a software subscription because it increases worker productivity by 20%.
Purchasing a luxury watch to convey a sense of prestige and status.
Purchasing bulk office supplies because of a 15% discount.
questions.explain: Emotional motives are based on feelings, social status, or prestige, whereas rational motives involve logic, saving money, or practical utility.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: When analyzing product features to assist in the selling process, why is it important to identify 'hidden benefits'?
options: Because they are illegal to advertise publicly.
Because the customer may not immediately realize these benefits just by looking at the product.
Because they allow salespeople to charge hidden fees.
Hidden benefits are generally considered a myth in marketing.
questions.explain: Hidden benefits are advantages not obvious from physical inspection. The salesperson must point them out so the customer fully understands the product's value.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: A car salesperson notes that a vehicle is equipped with anti-lock brakes (ABS) and 8 airbags. The primary rational buying motive related to these features is:
options: Prestige
Safety
Recreation
Vanity
questions.explain: Brakes and airbags are features whose main benefit is passenger safety, an entirely rational and practical buying motive.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA
